newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy rail chief says needs funds as wages at risk.
newsitem.headline: Italy rail chief says needs funds as wages at risk.

text.p: The head of Italian state rail company Ferrovie dello Stato (FS) said on Thursday the railway giant needed at least 1.4 trillion lire from the state or it risked not being able to pay employees' wages.

FS managing director Giancarlo Cimoli told the budget commission of the Italian lower house of parliament the lack of resources "will take the company into a cash deficit situation with heavy repercussions on investment and payments to employees and suppliers."

Cimoli said that between the government's 1997 budget and additional buidget deficit cutting measures taken in March this year, public funds made available to the railways had been reduced by 6.5 trillion lire.

Cimoli also said that 5.6 trillion lire of cash funds had not yet been transferred to the company and advances for write-downs of loans passed onto the state at the end of 1996 had only partially been reimbursed.
For that reason the rail company needed "to have access to at least 1.4 trillion lire of loans from the state to be able to guarantee operations and investiments," Cimoli said.

The government unveils its three-year plan of economic goals next week and Italian newspapers have reported in recent days the document could include spending cuts worth around 4.0 trillion lire in funds to state companies, including the railway giant.
